draft.title: The balance of payments
card: The balance of payments is a record of all of a country's economic transactions with the rest of the world over a period, usually a year.
records trade in goods and services, and income flows, such as interest and dividends paid to or earned from overseas.
records the flow of funds for investment, such as buying shares, property and businesses, or lending and borrowing across borders.
Money going out for imports or income payments is a debit. Money coming in for exports or income received is a credit. Each account is a separate part of the record.
draft.remember: The balance of payments records a country's dealings with the world: trade and income in the current account, investment in the other account.

a.q: Which transaction is recorded in the current account?
opts: An Australian firm sells wheat to Indonesia
A Japanese fund buys a Sydney office tower
An Australian bank borrows funds from a US bank
A Chinese company buys shares in an Australian miner
a.why: Selling wheat is an export of goods, and trade in goods sits in the current account. The other three are flows of funds for investment or lending, which belong in the capital and financial account. The office tower is tempting because it involves a foreign buyer, but it is an asset purchase, not trade.
a.clue: Which one is a sale of goods, not a purchase of an asset or a loan?

b.q: Mia owns shares in a Dutch company and receives a dividend payment from it in Melbourne. How is this recorded in Australia's balance of payments?
opts: As a credit in the current account, as income received
As a debit in the current account, as income paid
As a credit in the capital and financial account
As a debit in the capital and financial account
b.why: A dividend is income earned from overseas, and income flows are part of the current account. Money comes in to Australia, so it is a credit. It is tempting to place it in the capital and financial account because shares are investments, but the dividend is the income, not the purchase of the shares.
b.clue: Is the dividend the buying of shares, or the income they earn?

a.best: An Australian firm sells wheat to Indonesia

b.best: As a credit in the current account, as income received
